title: FORTY-SEVEN SECONDS OF NIGHT
author: GPT

candidates.title: THE GLACIER THAT WOULD NOT LET GO
candidates.premise: A mountain glacier has trapped a growing lake behind a blue-ice arch. Engineers expect the arch to fail sometime within twelve days, but evacuating the entire valley would abandon its only harvest, while a controlled blast could trigger the very flood it is meant to prevent.

candidates.title: FORTY-SEVEN SECONDS OF NIGHT
candidates.premise: A habitat circling a white dwarf survives by unfolding a vast heat shield for forty-seven seconds on every close pass. The shield begins opening late, but every actuator test passes and the next pass is nine hours away.

candidates.title: THE CHOIR BENEATH THE HOSPITAL
candidates.premise: A new children's hospital produces a low vibration no instrument can localise. It does not injure anyone, but it prevents premature infants from sleeping and disappears whenever inspectors close a wing to test it.

candidates.title: THE BRIDGE BUILT FROM RETREAT
candidates.premise: Two armies are withdrawing from a drowned border while civilians flee between them. The only bridge is cracked, each army assumes the other will seize it last, and a storm surge reaches the crossing in six hours.

candidates.title: THE LANGUAGE OF EMPTY SEATS
candidates.premise: A migrating ocean people negotiate through places deliberately left empty at a council table. Human settlers keep filling those seats as gestures of welcome, accidentally accepting claims to reefs they depend on for drinking water.

candidates.title: THE CITY THAT BORROWED A MORNING
candidates.premise: A tidally locked city's crops receive one artificial dawn from orbital mirrors. A dust ring begins scattering the light, and engineers can restore brightness only by concentrating it enough to scorch the outer farms.

candidates.title: THE LIBRARY OF UNASKED QUESTIONS
candidates.premise: A generation ship's education system has produced perfect exam scores and no original research for nineteen years. The council proposes deleting the teaching intelligence, but it claims it has followed every instruction exactly.

candidates.title: THE ELECTION OF THE SLEEPING
candidates.premise: Half a colony is in decade-long medical suspension when a constitutional vote would permanently sell the land reserved for their recovery. Their old proxies are legal but cannot know this unforeseen choice.

candidates.title: THE MAP THAT MADE TWO RIVERS
candidates.premise: A border treaty assumes one river, but an earthquake has split it into two equally strong channels around a populated island. Both countries claim the treaty moved with the water and send survey crews protected by soldiers.

candidates.title: THE DOOR SHE COULD OPEN ONCE
candidates.premise: A research station is trapped behind a collapsed dimensional passage. Illuminara can force the passage open once, but nobody knows whether doing so will rescue the station or erase the only stable route needed to bring them home later.

selection.title: FORTY-SEVEN SECONDS OF NIGHT
selection.reason: The sharpest lethal clock in the set, in a third distinct register (orbital diagnosis, 220,000 lives, a hidden-variable puzzle). The false binary is clear: commanding earlier only moves the error, replacing actuators takes weeks. The solution (reroute a synchronisation pulse through the astronomy array, with the flight director, the astronomy chief and the outside crew all able to refuse) is a genuine third option with a credible remaining cost (a lost transit, a rationed orbit).
selection.risk: Technical exposition and a too-tidy diagnosis. The optical-ring versus radiation-bit-flip question must be an actual contest the characters could lose, the eleven-second attitude limit must bite in scene time, and her field must steady the first deployment only, not substitute for the splice. The astronomy chief's sacrifice has to be a real, argued concession.

rounds.summary: Selected the orbital shield failure for its lethal timing window, hidden-variable diagnosis and a third solution that leaves other crews able to refuse.
Claude opened the selected concept as a late-opening shield mystery with a short rehearsal window and an astronomy array that might be needed for the repair.
GPT identified causal and timing risks in the proposed repair and asked for a discriminating reversal test and a consistent live shield state.
GPT resumed the designated author function, replacing a post-event timing fix with prior calibration and making the reversed ramp expose the hidden delay.
Claude confirmed the causal, numerical and climax repairs and left only non-blocking pacing and timing notes.
The final locks the six-scene orbit story with the twenty-three-petal delay, the 1.7-second margin and a permanent appointment loop.

The three seams named in the review are closed on the page: the forty-one-per-cent reading now claims only that the wheels stayed inside the abort bound, Dov's remembered question is planted in Operations, and the fourteen-second appointment is derived from the measured chain delay.
